title: Belly breathing lying down
goal: Feel the inhale go down into the belly while the chest and shoulders stay calm.
how: Lie on your back, knees bent, pillows under your head and knees.
One palm on the upper chest, the other below the ribs.
Inhale slowly through the nose so that only the lower palm rises.
Exhale through closed lips, gently drawing the belly in.
mistakes: Pushing the belly out with force.
dose: 5–10 minutes; the clinic suggests 3–4 times a day, later you can put a book on your belly.
source: Step-by-step technique lying and sitting, frequency

title: Belly breathing seated
goal: Transfer the skill from lying down to a working posture.
how: Sit on the edge of a chair, feet on the floor, shoulders and neck free.
Inhale through the nose — the belly moves into the palm.
Exhale through pursed lips, the belly returns.
mistakes: Holding the breath at the top of the inhale.
source: Section on the seated position

title: Test: “slouch vs ‘correct’ posture”
goal: Detect a habitual over-tensed “correct” stance.
how: Sing a couple of lines in your “best” posture.
Compare the ease of breathing and the sound.
Return to an upright posture, keeping the freedom found in the second version.
mistakes: Deciding to “sing slouched” — this is a diagnostic, not a recommendation.
source: D. S. Moore: pulling the shoulders back locks the ribs; describes the slouch test and work with mirrors

title: Singing in front of two mirrors
goal: See yourself from the side: a jutting head, a lifted chin.
how: Place two mirrors so your profile is visible.
Note whether the head moves forward or back on high notes.
dose: 2–3 minutes. In the app — front camera mode.
source: F. M. Alexander's method with mirrors

title: “The head doesn't reach forward”
goal: Remove pressure on the larynx from a jutting or tilted-back head.
how: Stand with weight evenly on both feet, knees not locked.
Imagine the crown of the head gently rising.
Don't lift the chin on high notes.
Sing a rising phrase, watching your chin.
mistakes: Pulling the chin in by force.
dose: As a check before every session.
source: A jutting or tilted-back head presses on the larynx; advice to free the legs

title: Constructive rest (semi-supine)
goal: Release general back and neck tension before practice.
how: Knees bent, feet on the floor.
A stack of books under your head (head not tilted back).
Lie “doing nothing”, noticing the support of your back.
Get up slowly, rolling onto your side.
mistakes: Head support too low or too high.
dose: 10–15 minutes (the duration is common practice; the source doesn't specify it).
source: Three essential elements: a firm surface, knees above the pelvis, support under the head

title: Clench and release the jaw
goal: Feel the difference between a clenched and a free jaw.
how: Clench your teeth hard for 3–5 seconds.
Notice the sensation; the tongue stays soft throughout.
mistakes: Tensing the neck along with the jaw.
source: Cambridge University Hospitals speech therapy leaflet

title: Stroking the jaw downward
goal: Let the jaw drop without effort.
how: Fingers on the sides of the face at the jaw joint.
The mouth opens by itself, lips barely touching.

title: Yawn-sigh
goal: Widen the throat and lower the larynx to a neutral position (Froeschels, 1952).
how: Yawn gently on an inhale through the mouth.
Repeat, then a sigh on “haaa” from top to bottom.
Move on to words starting with “h”.
mistakes: A yawn with a tense tongue (alternative — a “quiet” silent yawn).
source: Step-by-step description for speech therapists

title: “Whimpering puppy” and descent
goal: “Reset” the larynx — raise and lower it on a glissando.
how: A high hum in a small glissando, like a whimpering puppy, 3–4 times.
Slide down through the whole range to a low creaky sound.
On the fourth — a full rise and descent.
source: Section “laryngeal lift and lower”

title: Tongue: pointed ↔ wide
goal: Separate the work of the tongue tip and the tongue body.

title: The tongue writes in the air
goal: Tongue mobility and freedom.
how: Draw a picture in the air.
mistakes: Moving the head instead of the tongue.

title: Tongue “hump” forward
goal: Stretch the tongue root, which often presses on the larynx.
how: Push the “hump” forward without moving the tip.
mistakes: The tip slides out of place.

title: Tongue circling behind the lips
goal: Warm up the tongue and facial muscles.
how: Tongue tip between the teeth and lips.
source: Warm-up from City Academy (London)

title: Glissando with the tongue on the lip
goal: Stop the tongue pulling back while singing.
how: Rest the tongue on the lower lip.
Watch that the tongue doesn't creep back.
If needed, hold the tip with a tissue.
source: Lesson “Removing vocal strain”

title: Glissando with fingers on the cheeks
goal: Catch the jaw rising or clenching on high notes.
how: Fingertips on the cheeks at the joint.
Feel whether the jaw rises or clenches.
mistakes: Holding the jaw down with force.

title: Singing while moving the head
goal: Make sure the sound isn't held by the neck.
how: Slowly and continuously turn the head left and right.
Variant: stand still and massage the neck while singing.

title: Head turns and tilts (no full circles)
goal: Gentle neck mobility.
how: Slowly look left as far as is comfortable, then right.

title: Face stretch with a yawn
goal: Wake up the mouth and cheekbone muscles.
how: Tense and release the muscles around the mouth and cheekbones.

title: Full-body stretch, 10 seconds
goal: Prepare the body and posture for singing.
how: Reach your arms up, rise onto your toes.
source: «hold each stretch for 10 seconds»

title: Cool-down: descending SOVT glides
goal: Return the voice to speaking mode after a workload.
how: Soft descending glides on a lip trill or “mm” from the middle of the range down.
A yawn-sigh from top to bottom.
A few phrases of ordinary speech at a comfortable pitch.
mistakes: Going straight to shouting or noisy chatter.
source: Ragan's study page (singers rated the cool-down positively). Ragan's exact protocol is in a PDF whose text couldn't be extracted; the steps above follow common practice

title: Returning to speech after singing
goal: Don't leave the voice in “singing mode” for loud chatter.
how: Say 5–6 phrases calmly, at half voice (not a whisper!).
mistakes: Straight into a loud conversation in a noisy place.
source: On whispering

title: Humidify the air
goal: Don't dry out the mucous membranes, especially in winter.
how: If you don't have one — bowls of water by the radiators.
source: (bowls of water against dry air); (humidifier, nasal breathing); Temple Health (humidifier by the bed)

title: Instead of throat-clearing: a swallow / silent “cough”
goal: Don't injure the folds with frequent throat-clearing.
how: When you feel the urge, swallow hard or take a sip of water.
Or exhale silently with a puff of air.
If the urge is frequent, it's a reason to check for reflux.
mistakes: A sharp loud “ahem” out of habit.
dose: Every time you feel the urge.
source: (silent cough, swallow)

title: Voice rest without whispering
goal: Recovery when tired or ill without extra strain.
how: Don't whisper or speak loudly — both strain the voice.
Hoarseness lasting more than 2 weeks — see a doctor.
mistakes: “Whispering saves the voice” is a myth.
dose: As needed; 2 weeks is the threshold for seeing an ENT or voice doctor.
source: Temple Health — the 2-week rule

title: Caffeine, alcohol, smoking, late meals
goal: Remove factors that dry out and irritate the folds.
mistakes: Washing down a warm-up with coffee.
dose: A habit; in the app — a checklist.

title: Straw in water (bubbling)
goal: Maximum back-pressure and gentle closure without load.
how: A glass, water 2–5 cm deep, the straw in the water.
mistakes: Bursting bubbles from too much pressure.
source: Maxfield, Titze et al. 2014: a straw in water gives the highest intraoral pressure of 13 gestures

title: Narrow straw: an octave siren
goal: A stable SOVT effect (a narrow ~3.5 mm straw gives the most constant pressure).
how: Lips snug around a thin straw.
Slide from bottom to top like a siren.
A few times a day, 2–5 min each.
mistakes: Air escapes through the nose or the corners of the lips.
source: (narrow — the most stable pressures; wide in women — not); (Titze, NCVS/Utah introductory material)

title: Voiced “v” slide
goal: SOVT without props.
how: Lower lip to the upper teeth.
source: Voiced fricatives /v/, /z/ are among the 13 semi-occlusions

title: “Z” buzz on a triad
goal: SOVT with precise notes.
how: Tongue tip at the lower teeth.

title: Tongue “raspberry”
goal: Relaxing the lips and tongue + SOVT.
source: (raspberry is one of the 13 gestures)

title: VFE-1: a long “ee” on one note
goal: Endurance and efficient closure (Stemple protocol).
how: As long as possible, quiet and even.
mistakes: Stretching it out with a squeeze.
source: (protocol); review by Angadi, Croake, Stemple 2019 (J Voice)

title: VFE-2: “knoll” from bottom to top
goal: Stretching the folds, connecting to the top.

title: VFE-3: “knoll” from top to bottom
goal: A smooth descent through the registers.

title: VFE-4: “ol” on five notes
goal: The “power” component: long quiet notes C–D–E–F–G.
how: Each note as long as possible.
mistakes: The volume grows towards the end.

title: Resonant chant “mmee-mmee”
goal: Vibration “in the mask” with light closure (resonant voice therapy).
how: Hum with vibration at the lips and nose.
Open into a vowel without losing the sensation.
source: (LMRVT, Verdolini); (RCT of two SOVT protocols, Kapsner-Smith 2015)

title: Soft onset
goal: Airflow and closure starting together.
source: (figure 1 Onset/Offset); Miller “balanced onset” — table of contents

title: Aspirated onset “ha” → soft
goal: Remove tension through breathiness, then reduce the breathiness to zero.
mistakes: Air leaking through the whole note.
source: Three kinds of onset — (secondary source)

title: Light glottal onset
goal: Clear closure for breathy voices.
how: A very light “click” before the vowel.
source: Miller «hard attack»

title: Three onsets in a row
goal: Tell onsets apart and choose one.

title: Staccato onsets after Miller
goal: A balanced onset through short notes with breath release.
source: Section “Group 1 Exercises, Staccato and Onset” (our pattern). Unlike stacc-arp: one note, focus on the onset

title: Vowel modification ladder
goal: Evening out vowels towards the top (aggiustamento).
how: Round the lips slightly as you go up.
Return to “ah” on the way down.
source: (Miller, “Exercises for achieving aggiustamento”); (vowel neutralisation with pitch)

title: “Ah” with jaw opening (F1 tuning)
goal: Tune the first formant to the fundamental at the top (sopranos, above ~400–500 Hz).
how: Open the jaw more as the pitch rises.
source: Sopranos tune R1 to f0; the mouth opens as pitch rises

title: “Ee” → “ah” on one note
goal: Carry the brightness of “ee” into an open vowel.
how: Without moving the larynx, open to “ah”.
source: (a bright “ee” is the VFE starting position); the move to “ah” is teaching practice

title: “Ng-ah”: controlling the soft palate
goal: Conscious lifting of the velum (Estill Velum).
how: Open into “ah” — the palate is up.
Check: pinch your nose — the “ah” shouldn't change.
source: (Velum Control figure)

title: “Ya-ya-ya” with the tongue forward
goal: Release a retracted tongue root (Estill Tongue/Jaw).
how: Tongue tip at the lower teeth.
The tongue body works, the jaw stays still.
You can hold the jaw with a finger.

title: Thyroid tilt: a quiet “sob” upward
goal: A soft top without heaviness (Estill Thyroid tilt).
source: (Thyroid Cartilage Control; Sob quality). Unlike cvt-curbing and whimper: a sensation figure for the top, not a mode

title: Falsetto ↔ speech voice on one note
goal: Controlling the body-cover of the folds.
how: Switch to “thick” folds without changing the note.
source: (Body-Cover; Speech, Falsetto)

title: Arpeggio through the passaggio “oo→oh”
goal: Pass the primo/secondo passaggio without a click.
how: Move in semitones through the transition zone.
Men — modify towards “oo/oh” at the secondo passaggio.
source: (Miller: primo/secondo passaggio, zona di passaggio)

title: Full screening siren
goal: A continuous siren across the whole range; find where it breaks.
how: From the bottom to the very top and back.
Note where it breaks (marked in the UI).
mistakes: Treating a break as a failure.
source: (the siren as screening in EVT; secondary source). Unlike ng-siren: full range and diagnostics

title: Torso anchoring on the top note
goal: Stabilise the torso for the top (Estill Torso anchoring).
how: A slight widening of the back and ribs, as before lifting something heavy.
Hold it on the top note.
mistakes: Squeezing the belly and throat together.
source: (Torso, Head and Neck Control)

title: Crescendo on five notes
goal: Growing volume without raising the larynx.
how: The last one — an even f.
source: (messa di voce: soft → loud → soft; here half the skill on moving notes)

title: Diminuendo on the way down
goal: Keep support while fading.

title: Lamperti sequence
goal: Build agility on a foundation of messa di voce.
how: Messa di voce on the tonic.
mistakes: Rushing to the scale without an even messa di voce.
source: (Lamperti's order: messa di voce, intervals, scales, arpeggios, trill)

title: Pulses at ~5 Hz
goal: Find a vibrato rate of 5–7 Hz through even pulses.
how: Slow pitch pulses of a semitone.
Let go of control — let the oscillation run by itself.
mistakes: Pulsing with volume or the belly (“bleating”).
An extent wider than a semitone.
source: (5–7 Hz, extent 6–8%)

title: Even vibrato on long notes
goal: Vibrato regularity — this is what improves with training.
how: An even vibrato on every note.
mistakes: Vibrato only on the last note.
source: (Mitchell & Kenny 2010: regularity and extent grow, not rate)

title: Thirds (Vaccai lesson 1b theme)
goal: Clean legato thirds.
source: (1a — the scale “Manca sollecita”, 1b — thirds); — score. The notes are not Vaccai's melody

title: Fourths and fifths (lesson 2)
goal: Accurate intonation of wide intervals without glissando.
how: Hear the top note in advance.
Take it from above, don't “slide in”.

title: Sixths, sevenths, octaves (lessons 3–4)
goal: Wide leaps in one position.
mistakes: A hit on the top note.
source: Unlike octave-jump: a sequence of widening intervals

title: Semitones (lesson 5)
goal: Chromatic precision.
mistakes: Going flat on the way down.

title: Appoggiatura from above and below (lesson 8a)
goal: An expressive suspension without scooping.

title: Mordent (lesson 9)
goal: A quick, clear ornamental note.
how: Lightness from the larynx, not the belly.

title: Gruppetto (lesson 10)
goal: An even four-note turn.
how: Hold the main note at the end.

title: Trill preparation (lesson 11)
goal: Gradually build a whole-tone trill.
mistakes: An extent wider than a tone.
source: (the trill is Lamperti's last step)

title: Octave roulade (lessons 7, 12)
goal: Fluency over an octave up and down.
source: Unlike rossini: sixteenths, both sides of the octave

title: Portamento (lesson 13)
goal: A stylish legato carry without wailing.
how: Slide at the last moment before the note.

title: Cantabile phrase (Concone)
goal: A singing legato in the middle register.
source: “for the middle of the voice”. Notes — our pattern

title: Even sustained notes (Marchesi Op. 1)
goal: Even out the timbre across the scale.
how: The same colour on every note.
source: The score couldn't be opened; the pattern is ours

title: “Necessary twang” on vowels
goal: A slight narrowing of the aryepiglottic funnel as a constant base (not a bright twang).
how: Find the “nya” twang (already in the catalogue).

title: Saving support for the end of the phrase
goal: Don't spend support early; save it for the top and the end of the phrase.
how: Full support on the last note.
mistakes: “Breathing out” everything on the first note.

title: Lip trill (brrr)
goal: Release tension in the lips, jaw and tongue; connect sound with breath.
how: Lips gently closed; you can lightly hold your cheeks with your fingers.
Add voice on a comfortable note.
Do a glissando up and down.

title: Pucker — smile
goal: Mobility and springiness of the lips.

title: Lip training on “p-b-m”
goal: Clear labial consonants without the jaw.
how: Jaw still; you can hold it with your hand.
Then a third up and down.

title: Tongue independent of the jaw (“la-la”)
goal: Separate tongue and jaw: they use different muscles.
how: “La-la-la” with the tongue tip behind the upper teeth.
mistakes: The jaw bounces on every syllable.

title: Spatula — needle
goal: Control of tongue shape.
how: Lay a wide relaxed tongue on the lower lip (5 s).
Narrow the tongue and stick it out to a point (5 s).

title: Cup / tongue to the upper lip
goal: Raising the tongue tip (needed for “r”, “l”, “t”).
how: A wide tongue on the lower lip.
Raise it to the upper lip.

title: Mushroom and clicks (horse)
goal: Stretch the frenulum, strengthen the tongue body.
how: Suck the whole tongue up to the palate.
Hold 5–10 s, slowly opening the mouth.
A series of clicks in rhythm.
mistakes: The tongue comes away at the sides.

title: Tongue circling behind the lips
goal: Release tension in the tongue root.
how: Trace a circle around the front of the mouth with the tongue tip.

title: A free jaw (massage and “heavy jaw”)
goal: Remove tension in the chewing muscles and a “white” sound.
how: Massage the chewing muscles near the jaw joint with your fingers.
The jaw “hangs” under its own weight.
Check with your hand that the jaw doesn't move forward.

title: Find the soft palate (Hung-ah)
goal: Feel the soft palate and the tongue body close and part.
how: A mirror and a torch, mouth open.
If it doesn't work, start a yawn: the palate rises by itself.
mistakes: A forced yawn with a tight larynx.

title: Holding the palate for 4 counts
goal: Control the palate, remove nasality.
how: Lift the soft palate (the start of a yawn).
Repeat, then sing “ah” with the palate raised.

title: “Ka-ga” and “ng-ah”: the tongue body
goal: Precise velar consonants and separating the tongue from the palate.
how: “ng-ah” (from the velar nasal into an open vowel).
At the end the palate is up, the tongue lies loose, with space between them.
mistakes: The sound goes into the nose.

title: Rolled “r”
goal: Keep the tongue tip active, train the vibration.
how: “d-d-d” with the tongue tip behind the teeth, faster.

title: Long vowel, short consonant
goal: The principle of sung diction: the vowel is sustained, consonants are quick and clear.
how: Take a phrase from a song.
Put the consonants back without shortening the vowels.

title: Consonant before the beat
goal: The vowel lands right on the beat, the rhythm doesn't “lag”.
how: The vowel right on the click.
Apply it to a line of a song.
mistakes: Consonants on the beat (the vowel is late).

title: Clean vowels A-E-I-O-U without the jaw
goal: Clear vowels with a stable larynx and a free jaw.
how: “ah-eh-ee-oh-oo”: only the tongue and lips change shape.
The jaw almost still (check with a finger).

title: Whispered, but clear
goal: Articulation without relying on volume.
how: The song's lyrics in a light whisper (no forced hissing).
Every consonant is heard across the room.
Then the same in a piano voice.
mistakes: A forced whisper (strains the folds) — keep it light and short.

title: “Red leather, yellow leather…”
goal: R/L, clean liquids.
how: Sing it on one note, then on a triad.
source: (traditional English)

title: “Betty Botter bought a bit of butter”
goal: B/T for English repertoire.
source: (19th-century verse, public domain)
